title: This week in PC games: start a new life in Vice City, escape a dying universe before the last black hole evaporates, and avenge your pigeon with a sledgehammer
excerpt: Rockstar life sims, black holes, spirit mountains, chatty pickles, witch battles, and a Zelda-ish take on Vice City - the latest PC releases, as curated by RPS.
content:
What we're feeding the Maw

Happy this week, all! Please throw yourself upon the floor in consternation, clawing at your face and hair, for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is nigh. In just a few short days, every gaming vertical under the sun will be publishing features about the exact depth of Jason Duval's ripped abs and what this Says About America Today, or how many bottle caps you must gather to unlock Lucia Caminos' Gundam mode.

Fortunately for my sanity, Rockstar's crime colossus isn't yet nigh on PC, though the word is that modders driven nuts by Claude will soon be along with an unofficial "port". As such, while we do have a few Grandiosely Thievish articles in store this week – not least, coverage of the on-going unionisation situation at Rockstar – we can afford to spend a few hours writing about non-GTA things. The appraisal of mushrooms, for example, or the solubility of rubber hosing, or the parrying of spells. Without further ado, here's this week's uncommonly flavourful crop of new PC games. Don't worry, dear Maw. You'll get to eat Jason eventually.

Monday 16th November

  • Utopium is a top-down brawler in which you and your sledgehammer rampage through an enormous, bizarre factory, seeking to avenge your dead pigeon pal. You can dislodge the very souls of your foes with your hammer, smashing their ectoplasmic selves into other enemies. Videogames!
  • Spirit Crossing is a laidback MMO-ish attraction from the makers of Triple Town and Cozy Grove. Design a home on a mountain peak, befriending local spirits. Other players appear as shadows, till you bring them into your game with a high five.
  • Feed the Maw? Nay, you shall Feed the Vessel, this being a short incremental game about growing human clones and tossing their bits to the horrible god lurking in your ship's hold.
  • Etch is roguelite Pac-Man, with a bunch of abilities, upgrades and gadgets to grease your conquering of some colourful block mazes.
  • Here Comes The Horde is an autobattler set in King Richard's day that allows you to pit thousands of pitchfork-wielding commoners against thousands of living dead.
  • Temple of the Machine God is an esoteric first-person escape game in which you are trying to flee a dead universe. You wake up on a superstructure orbiting a black hole, built by robots left behind by humans who've fled to another dimension. Search for the exit, before the black hole disintegrates. Be wary of "entropic cats".

Tuesday 17th November

  • Steel Gullet is a factory puzzler set aboard a mobile mechanised city, in which your job is to sift and process the waste of the world before. You will have to think about density, elasticity, solubility, melting, and boiling, while deciding whether to help or hinder the local resistance organisation. I like this one's vibe.
  • Okurek is a short game about working a farm in 1980s Bohemia, pickling cucumbers, talking to your pickled cucumbers, trying not to talk to your pickled cucumbers, and dealing with the weird purple rot that's gunking up the mountain scenery. Seemingly, it's a game about grieving. There is a deer prophet who speaks in rhyme.

Wednesday 18th November

  • Vice: Magic City Mayhem (pictured) is a top-down 80s pixel fantasy featuring laser-breathing raptors, cool jackets, and dungeons inspired by Zelda. It's got nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.
  • Korridor is a scrolling vertical dungeon shooter featuring an electro-metal soundtrack and some actual medieval celebs. It's inspired by those mobile games you keep seeing ads for on Youtube.
  • Toto's Journey is a jaunty 3D action adventure in which Dorothy's pooch bounds around Oz solving logic puzzles and mastering magic. We're not in, er, Canonical Kansas (Canonsas?) any more, Toto!

Thursday 19th November

  • It's time for this week's barn-storming release: Fungarium, in which you try to distinguish toxic from edible mushrooms, each brought to you by hungry villagers during a potato blight. Who will you send home hungry? Who will you accidentally poison? The game cautions you that it isn't a guide to identifying real-life fungus. Personal insight: mushrooms are lying bastards. The tastiest ones almost always seem to have a deadly twin.
  • Witch the Showdown is an anime boss-rush deckbuilder in which parrying attacks earns you mana for your cards.

Friday 20th November

  • Sure, you could start a rock band, or you could play the booze, cigs and piss-fuelled Rock Band Simulator - the My Summer Car of rhythm-bashing music games. Where is Brendy? Come back Brendy and review this.
  • Vela is a solitaire variant based on 1991's Heaven & Earth, remade with the permission of the original dev.
  • People who like bullet hells and programmer passion projects - Behelade may be your jam. It was "programmed the old-school way, in the C language and without a full game engine", and is a whopping 10MB in size.
  • Another oldie: Theocracy is an RTS and city builder from 2000 in which you command an Aztec leader who must unify the tribes to repel the invading Spanish. This week's re-release updates it to run on Windows 10 and 11.

GTA and new PC releases aside, this week will see the first instalment of our annual wrestle to determine the 100 best PC games. So much blood has been spilled, so many friendships destroyed, so many Civilization games hurled upon a pyre and danced around, screaming Latin curses… and now we have to deal with all of your bad opinions in the comments.

Why would you put us through this madness, Julian?? Oh nuts, he's gone on holiday. In Julian's absence, James is presiding over the GTApocalypse alongside the rollout of various chunky freelance features. Mark, meanwhile, has somehow found time to become the Pope while reporting on labour action at Rockstar. I myself have dire plans for Vice City, but I'm also going back to Subnautica 2, ahead of the next major early access update. How about you? Will you be getting your fill of Jason and Lucia on that console you're even now trying to surreptitiously kick behind the sofa? Or are you more taken by the prospect of examining toadstools?
